body:
I've tried three different gamepads under Windows using USB cable. The `serial number` is unavailable. 

Perhaps this can be improved at some point through another pull request that can reliably identify the gamepads.

```
Godot Engine v4.6.rc.gh-113873.5ee8ccaad (2026-01-16 19:11:19 UTC) - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL API 3.3.0 Core Profile Context 25.12.1.251128 - Compatibility - Using Device: ATI Technologies Inc. - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics

Found joypad #0: XInput Controller - 0300fa675e0400008e02000014017801
{ "raw_name": "Xbox 360 Controller", "vendor_id": "1118", "product_id": "654", "xinput_index": "0" }
+ Found newly connected joypad #0: XInput Controller - 0300fa675e0400008e02000014017801

- Disconnected joypad #0.
+ Found newly connected joypad #0: NVIDIA SHIELD Controller - 030028b6550900001472000025056800
{ "raw_name": "NVIDIA SHIELD Controller", "vendor_id": "2389", "product_id": "29204", "xinput_index": "0" }

- Disconnected joypad #0.
+ Found newly connected joypad #0: XInput Controller - 0300fa675e040000ff02000000007801
{ "raw_name": "Xbox One Controller", "vendor_id": "1118", "product_id": "767", "xinput_index": "0" }

```

Tested with a DualShock 4 on Windows 11, it works as expected, code looks good to me!
```
PS4 Controller 03008fe54c050000cc09000000016800
{ "raw_name": "PS4 Controller", "vendor_id": "1356", "product_id": "2508", "serial_number": "dc-af-68-33-9b-85", "xinput_index": "0" }
```

Personally, I'm not entirely sure how useful it is to get a serial number of a controller in a game though😅Please let me know if you feel it's useful!

Be sure to add the patch to the thirdparty README:
```diff
 - `0006-fix-cs-environ.patch` ([GH-109283](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109283))
+- `0008-fix-linux-joycon-serial-num.patch` ([GH-113873](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113873))
 
```
